title: Lagrange: An Open-Vocabulary, Energy-Based Sparse Framework for Generalized End-to-End Driving
abstract: arXiv:2606.20274v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Scaling end-to-end autonomous driving to complex, open-world environments requires perceptual models that generalize to anomalous scenarios and planners that produce kinematically valid trajectories. Existing paradigms face a distinct dichotomy between representational efficiency and generalization capacity. Dense models (e.g., occupancy networks), while geometrically robust, incur critical computational bottlenecks and struggle with high-level semantic reasoning. Conversely, sparse, query-based planners are efficient but reliant on closed-set definitions, rendering them vulnerable to out-of-distribution (OOD) events. translated_title: Lagrange：一种面向广义端到端驾驶的开放词汇、基于能量的稀疏框架
translated_abstract: 将端到端自动驾驶扩展到复杂的开放世界环境，需要能够泛化到异常场景的感知模型以及能够生成运动学有效轨迹的规划器。现有范式在表示效率和泛化能力之间存在明显分歧。密集模型（例如占用网络）虽然在几何上稳健，但会引发关键的计算瓶颈，并难以进行高层语义推理。相反，稀疏的基于查询的规划器效率高，但依赖于封闭集定义，使其容易受到分布外（OOD）事件的影响。尽管最近的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型提供了开放词汇推理，但其自回归、离散的令牌生成方式从根本上与车辆动力学所需的连续、高频控制要求相冲突。为解决这一问题，我们提出了Lagrange，一种开放词汇、计算稀疏的驾驶框架。
tldr: 本文提出Lagrange，一个结合开放词汇推理与能量基稀疏规划的框架，旨在解决端到端自动驾驶中密集模型计算瓶颈和稀疏模型泛化不足的冲突，并克服VLA模型离散生成与连续控制需求的不匹配。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Lagrange, a framework combining open-vocabulary reasoning with energy-based sparse planning, to resolve the conflict between dense model computational bottlenecks and sparse model generalization limitations in end-to-end driving, while overcoming the mismatch between VLA discrete generation and continuous control needs.
